Through targeted separation and identification of complex components in AE using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography with quadrupole orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-Q-orbitrap-HRMS), we identified β,β-dimethyl-acryl-alkannin (DMAA) as a novel β-gal inhibitor. The pharmacodynamic effects of this compound were validated through in vitro cellular imaging using senescent cell and foam cell models, real-time in vivo fluorescence tracking in zebrafish models of AS, and histopathological analysis using apolipoprotein E-deficient ( ApoE −/− ) mice with high-fat-diet-induced AS. The findings confirmed the therapeutic potential of DMAA in mitigating senescence-associated vascular dysfunction. This study comprehensively evaluated the use of β-gal–based probes and natural compounds to suppress aging-related processes, highlighting their therapeutic implications for AS and other aging-associated diseases.

title: Preparation and collaborative study of a recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) genome copy number reference material
Rapid adulteration detection of herbal powder using AI-driven multiple digital fingerprints: A case of Bajiaohuixiang (Illicium verum Hook. f.)
abstract: Herbal powder, a common dosage form in traditional Chinese medicine, requires rigorous authenticity assessment to ensure medicinal quality and therapeutic efficacy. In this study, we proposed an artificial intelligence (AI) assisted digital fingerprint strategy for rapid detection of herbal powder adulteration, using Bajiaohuixiang (BJHX) as a case. The intelligent algorithms combined with digital image recognition (DIR) and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) techniques achieved effective discrimination in both binary and seven-class classification of adulteration. The optimized bidirectional long short-term memory network delivered good performance, which achieved accuracies of 96.11% and 80.00% using the DIR dataset, and 94.44% and 88.10% using the NIRS dataset, for binary and seven-class classification, respectively. Multimodal data fusion significantly enhanced performance, yielding classification accuracies of 97.22% and 91.90% for the two tasks, respectively, and a quantitative model with coefficient of determination of 0.8807, root mean square error of 0.0560, and mean absolute error of 0.0443. The strategy's robustness was confirmed through external validation, where only one out of multiple commercial and laboratory-prepared samples was flagged as potentially adulterated. Furthermore, greenness assessment using Analytical Greenness Calculator (AGREE, 0.92), Analytical Greenness Metric of Sample Preparation (AGREEprep, 0.90), and Blue Applicability Grade Index (BAGI, 80) frameworks confirmed its environmental sustainability and practical applicability. Overall, this work highlights the significant potential of integrating AI with DIR and NIRS as a rapid, accurate, and green tool for herbal powder authentication.

title: Natural products in insomnia: Molecular mechanisms, action targets, and therapeutic potential
abstract: Insomnia is a disorder characterized by sleep disturbances and daytime impairments. It can be alleviated with conventional clinical medications, but considerable individual variability and adverse effects (AEs) remain persistent challenges. Many natural products are known for their low toxicity and multi-target properties. These products offer distinct advantages in treating insomnia by modulating its underlying pathological mechanisms. Although previous reviews have summarized the effects of natural products on insomnia, systematic classification based on natural products and comprehensive exploration of their interactions with multidimensional pathological mechanisms remain insufficient. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms by which natural products modulate insomnia. It also offers an in-depth discussion of the current limitations and challenges. The goal is to establish a theoretical foundation and technical framework to optimize treatment strategies and advance the clinical translation of natural product research.

title: Targeting SEC23A: Artesunate's dual pathway approach to reversing gastric metaplasia
abstract: : Artesunate (ART) is a promising multi-target drug, yet its efficacy and mechanism against intestinal metaplasia (IM)/spasmolytic polypeptide-expressing metaplasia (SPEM), a key precancerous gastric lesion with no effective therapy, remain unexplored. This work presented that ART reversed SPEM and IM progression in mice, selectively impairing IM cell viability via inducing paraptosis. Mechanically, ART triggered paraptosis through dual pathways, involving reactive oxygen species (ROS)-dependent c-jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) / P38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) activation and ROS-independent endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress via direct SEC23A binding. ART disrupted SEC23A-SEC24A dimer formation, inducing ER stress via promoting K63-linked ubiquitination and p62-mediated autophagic degradation of SEC23A. Moreover, its efficacy was confirmed in human-derived IM organoids, showing reduced growth, SEC23A degradation, and MAPK/ER stress activation. Taken together, ART alleviates gastric precancerous lesions by selectively inducing paraptosis through ROS-dependent JNK/P38 MAPK activation and SEC23A-targeted ER stress via coatomer protein complex II (COPII) disruption and autophagic degradation.

title: Ultra-high-throughput metabolic stability assay powered by acoustic ejection mass spectrometry with sample-specific MS/MS methods
A quantitative screening strategy based on activity-content ratio for prioritizing bioactive compounds in medicinal plants
abstract: of 15.21 ± 1.23 μM. The consistent performance of the ACR model across two distinct enzymatic targets and chemical families (alkaloids and flavonoids) demonstrates its reliability and broad applicability. This study provides a reliable and efficient quantitative tool for bioactivity evaluation, which is expected to greatly accelerate the discovery and quality control of bioactive medicinal plants.

title: Ambient ionization mass spectrometry imaging in pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis: Advances and transformative perspectives
Flexible adipocytes guided nano-anchoring medicine: A precision therapeutic strategy for obesity
A naturally occurring coumestan dolichosin A targets Syk kinase to dually inhibit macrophage inflammation and osteoclast formation for anti-arthritic therapy
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by synovial inflammation and osteoclast-mediated bone destruction. Current therapeutic strategies often lack dual efficacy in targeting both inflammatory and bone-eroding pathways. In this study, we investigated the anti-arthritic properties and underlying mechanisms of dolichosin A (DoA), a naturally occurring coumestan derived from Glycine tabacina (Labill.) Benth. DoA administration was found to significantly block lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammatory activation of macrophages and inhibit receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) ligand (RANKL)-induced formation of osteoclasts. This dual effect significantly contributed to the alleviation of inflammation and bone destruction in collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mice treated with DoA. DoA directly targeted spleen tyrosine kinase (Syk), with hydrogen bonds formed with Glu452, Asn499, and Asp512 playing a critical role in its binding to Syk. DoA inhibited the autophosphorylation of Syk and activation of downstream signaling pathways, including phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), and calcium oscillations, thereby exerting inhibitory effects on macrophage inflammation and osteoclast formation. Additionally, it was found that the combination of the natural Syk inhibitor DoA with the Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor tofacitinib (TOF) resulted in an enhanced anti-arthritic effect in the CIA mice. Furthermore, DoA was loaded into a folic acid (FA)-functionalized liposomal delivery system (DoA@FA-Lips), which significantly enhanced the pharmacological effects of DoA with low cytotoxicity. Our findings highlight DoA as a novel dual-functional agent targeting Syk to concurrently mitigate macrophage-driven inflammation and osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, offering a promising strategy for RA therapy.

title: AI-powered generative mRNA design: GEMORNA enables efficient expression and delivery for next-generation RNA therapeutics
Cyclovirobuxine D suppresses gastric cancer growth by targeting the V-ATPase complex and inducing excessive endo-lysophagy
abstract: Gastric cancer is one of the most malignant cancers in the world, posing a significant threat to human life and persisting as a major clinical challenge. Cyclovirobuxine D (CVB-D), derived from boxwood and traditionally employed in cardiovascular disease treatment, has emerged as a promising candidate for cancer therapy. However, its mechanism of action still needs to be clearly defined. We aimed to comprehensively evaluate CVB-D's impact on gastric cancer and elucidate its underlying mechanisms. Here, we found CVB-D induced excessive endo-lysophagy in gastric cancer. Moreover, multi-omics analysis revealed that CVB-D directly engages the ATP6V0A1-containing V-ATPase complex and perturbs endo-lysosomal homeostasis, leading to abnormal lysosomal acidification, impaired lysosomal protease activity, and autophagic flux blockade. Mechanistically, damaged endo-lysosomes recruited the autophagic adaptor P62/SQSTM1 in a galectin-8-dependent manner, ultimately triggering endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and apoptosis in gastric cancer cells. Furthermore, through cell-derived xenograft (CDX) and patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models, we validated the therapeutic efficacy of CVB-D against gastric cancer. Notably, CVB-D enhances the sensitivity of gastric cancer to the chemotherapeutic agent cisplatin. Our findings suggest that CVB-D holds promise as an effective therapeutic agent for gastric cancer treatment.

title: Carbon dots derived from natural medicines: Therapeutic advances and challenges
abstract: Carbon dots (CDs) are a novel nanomaterial exhibiting exceptional biocompatibility, tunable fluorescence, and versatile functionality, making them a promising candidate in biomedicine. Natural medicines, including plants, animals, minerals, and their extracts, represent ideal precursors for CD synthesis due to their abundance, renewability, and eco-friendliness. This addresses sustainability and environmental concerns associated with conventional chemical precursors. Natural medicine-derived CDs (NM-CDs) feature quasi-spherical core-shell structures, ranging from 1 to 10 nm, with surface hydroxyl, carboxyl, and amino groups enhancing their hydrophilicity and functionality. Their properties can be further modulated by synthesis temperature and heteroatom doping. Critically, NM-CDs combine the pharmacological activities of natural medicines with the unique nanoscale properties of CDs, bridging traditional medicine and modern nanotechnology. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the development of NM-CDs, including green natural precursors, formation mechanisms, and synthesis strategies. It systematically analyzes the structure and properties of NM-CDs, categorizes their therapeutic applications into seven major disease types, and offers a detailed explanation of their fundamental pharmacological mechanisms. Finally, ten key opportunities and challenges for the sustainable development of NM-CDs are highlighted. By integrating efficient resource utilization, green chemistry principles, and clinical demands, NM-CDs exhibit strong potential to advance bio-based nanotherapeutics and enhance the value of natural medicines through modern scientific approaches.

title: Editorial Board
Self-assembled nanovesicles integrated patch mediated transdermal delivery of Chinese medicinal formula alleviates insomnia with high safety
abstract: Insomnia, a prevalent neurological disease, is characterized by neurotransmitter disorder, inflammation and oxidative stress. Current treatments are often limited in efficacy due to their single-target regulatory mechanisms. YiNianJin (YNJ) is a classical formula that employs multiple therapeutic effects in treating insomnia. However, conventional oral delivery of YNJ formula is challenged by notable limitations, including Hg 2+ accumulation released from cinnabar, limited bioavailability of active constituents, that resulted in both of the toxicity issue and limited therapeutic efficacy. To address these multiple obstacles, we developed a peptide self-assembled penetrating nanovesicles integrated within a controlled releasing matrix, forming into YNJ patch (YNJP). Cinnabar is encapsulated within nanovesicles functionalized with cell-penetrating (YGRKKRRQRRR, TAT) and intestinal wall-penetrating (CSKSSDYQC, CSK) peptides, forming TAT/CSK-cinnabar vesicles (TCCV), and integrated into a controlled-release polymeric matrix, loaded with other herbal components, forming into a hybrid patch. YNJP is shown to significantly enhance the sequential penetration of cinnabar across the stratum corneum (SC), abdominal fat, and small intestinal wall, along with the obvious efficacy in the transdermal delivery of other herbal components. Compared with the conventional oral delivery of YNJ, YNJP significantly reduced the Hg 2+ accumulation in major organs by 58.3%–85.8%. In addition to inhibit the inflammation and oxidative stress to relieve insomnia, YNJP can also restore the brain-gut axis mediated serotonin (5-HT) release and 5-HT1A receptors (5-HT1AR) activation, representing a safe and innovative transdermal delivery platform for Chinese formulae containing both multiple homogenous components and toxic compound, as well as offering a new Chinese medicine scheme for the treatment of complex disorders such as insomnia with high efficiency and biosafety.

title: AI-Driven Delivery of Psychobiotics: Enhancing Targeted Treatments of the Gut-Brain Axis and Prospects for Personalized Applications
abstract: Psychobiotics are beneficial microorganisms or their metabolites that modulate the gut microbiome to enhance mental health. However, the oral delivery of live bacteria faces several challenges, including inactivation by gastric acid, low intestinal colonization rates, poor targeting, and considerable interindividual variability in efficacy, which impede their clinical translation. This study focuses on artificial intelligence (AI)-driven psychobiotic nanodelivery systems. Initially, it summarizes common psychobiotics and their mechanisms targeting the gut-brain axis for treating psychiatric disorders. It then outlines the main types of probiotic delivery systems and their applications in mental health treatment. Furthermore, the significant role of artificial intelligence in strain selection and optimization, personalized treatment design, and clinical outcome evaluation is explored. Finally, the study anticipates the prospects and challenges of integrating artificial intelligence with nanodelivery systems to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of psychobiotics, aiming to provide valuable insights for related research and clinical applications.

title: AI-driven classification and distinction of indoleamine and tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase inhibitors by analysis of molecular electrostatic maps
Recent advances and expanding applications of organoid models in unveiling drug ADME profiles
abstract: models generated from stem or progenitor cells that closely replicate the structural and functional complexity of human organs. These systems are emerging as powerful tools in pharmacokinetic research, addressing key limitations of traditional models such as two-dimensional (2D) cell cultures and animal experiments, which are often constrained by physiological mismatch and species-specific differences. This review summarizes recent advances in the development of organoid models, with a focus on hepatic and intestinal systems, and highlights their application in studying drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME). We discuss how organoids improve predictions of oral bioavailability, facilitate assessment of drug-drug interactions (DDI), and help interpret interindividual pharmacokinetic variability. Current challenges including incomplete functional maturation, lack of standardization, and limited vascularization are also considered. Finally, we explore future directions involving the integration of organoids with advanced microphysiological systems (such as organ-on-a-chip (OoC)) and artificial intelligence (AI). With ongoing refinement, organoid-based approaches are expected to significantly improve the efficiency of drug development and the accuracy of clinical translation, paving the way for advances in precision pharmacology and personalized medicine.

title: Intracellular SPP1 inhibits FNDC5 to activate DEGS1-regulated ceramide metabolism in silicosis
abstract: Silicosis is an irreversible occupational disease, but its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Although secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1) and lipid dysregulation have been implicated in silicosis, their functional interplay is unclear. In this study, we demonstrated that macrophage-specific Spp1 knockout in mice attenuated silica-induced pulmonary fibrosis, improved lung function, and suppressed aberrant lipid metabolism both in vivo and in vitro . Specifically, silica-induced intracellular SPP1 (iSPP1) regulated the ceramide synthesis pathway by promoting the ubiquitination of fibronectin type III domain-containing 5 (FNDC5). This action attenuated FNDC5-mediated ubiquitination and subsequent downregulation of Δ4-dihydroceramide desaturase 1 (DEGS1), a key enzyme in de novo ceramide synthesis within the endoplasmic reticulum. Overall, we identified the interaction of SPP1, FNDC5, and DEGS1, providing a mechanistic basis and a potential therapeutic strategy for targeting lipid dysregulation in silicosis.

title: Application of chemometrics based on digital images and deep learning for analyzing quality of Magnolia officinalis cortex during sweating processing
abstract: The traditional processing method of “sweating processing” is one of the key origin factors contributing to the quality formation of authentic Chinese herbal medicines, which is closely related to unique quality and clinical efficacy. Magnolia officinalis cortex (MOC) is the dried bark of Magnolia officinalis Rehd. et Wils to treat gastrointestinal diseases. The 2025 edition of Chinese Pharmacopoeia stipulates that MOC must undergo sweating processing until the inner surface turns purplish-brown or brown. However, quality assessment methods for MOC remain constrained by subjective biases or complex instruments, thereby impacting reproducibility and cost-effectiveness. Therefore, this study proposed a method based on digital images and deep learning to analyze color characteristics and monitor dynamic changes during the sweating processing of MOC. In this study, one-class classification was used to correctly authenticate and recognize the category of MOC samples at different stages of sweating. Pearson correlation analysis examined obvious correlations between color frequency histograms and indicator components of MOC samples. Furthermore, the study established regression prediction models including magnolol and honokiol based on partial least squares regression (PLSR) and successive projections algorithm-PLSR (SPA-PLSR). Importantly, this study confirmed the great potential of residual neural network-50 (ResNet-50) based on convolutional neural network (CNN) in understanding the quality formation during sweating processing of MOC by utilizing more stable SPA-PLSR ( R 2 Pred>0.75, RPD>2). In conclusion, the method provided new ideas and approaches to evaluate quality control of sweating processing for MOC and offered a reference for monitoring the processing of other Chinese herbal medicines.

title: AI for TCM: From target identification to drug design
abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) achieves therapeutic effects through multi-component and multi-target regulation, but its complexity makes mechanistic interpretation and rational prescription optimization difficult. The rapid growth of chemical structure data, multi-omics profiles, and large-scale clinical records has facilitated data-driven TCM research, although it also presents significant analytical challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a solution to this data-to-knowledge gap. This review covers recent progress in AI-driven TCM research, from active ingredient and target discovery to mechanism elucidation and intelligent prescription recommendations. We highlight AI-assisted compound screening and structure-based target prediction, integration of multi-omics data and knowledge graphs (KGs) for network inference, and AI-based prediction of synergistic drug combinations and formula optimization. Finally, we discuss key challenges related to data quality, interpretability, robustness, and clinical translation, along with future directions in AI-driven TCM research.

title: ACAP-AG: A graph neural network model for anticancer activity prediction by integrating heterogeneous data
Nanoscale renaissance of glycyrrhizic acid: Bridging phytochemistry with functional material innovation
abstract: Transforming herbal-derived small molecules into nano-formulations represents a crucial interdisciplinary strategy for modernizing traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). Glycyrrhizic acid (GL), renowed for its well-documented clinical efficacy and intrinsic amphiphilic structure, exemplifies the successful conversion of TCM compounds into functional nanobiomaterials. A systematic analysis of GL’s extensive evolution from a therapeutic agent to a multifunctional biomaterial is critical to accelerating TCM modernization, yet remains insufficiently reviewed. In this article, we comprehensively reconstruct and elucidate GL’s evolutionary trajectory from a conventional pharmacological molecule to an advanced nanobiomaterial. First, we analyze the molecular structure of GL alongside its in vivo metabolic pathways. Next, we summarize the diverse pharmacological activities of GL as a small-molecule drug. Subsequently, we trace the development of GL-based biomaterials over the past five decades, classifying them into six principal categories: nanoparticles, micelles, hydrogels, liposomes, metal-organic frameworks, and nanocrystals (NCs). Each category is further subdivided and systematically analyzed. We provide an in-depth discussion from multiple perspectives, including GL’s self-assembly behavior, ligand functionalities, and potential for biointerface modulation, covering aspects such as preparation methods, design principles, performance advantages, and current limitations. Finally, grounded in clinical translational needs, we identify current challenges, propose feasible solutions, and outline future research directions for GL-based biomaterials.

title: CAF-mediated compartmentalized dual POSTN–ITGB8 axis drives Osimertinib resistance in lung adenocarcinoma
abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) represents a histological subtype of lung cancer with substantial disease burden. A particularly prominent feature in Asian populations is the exceptionally high incidence of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations. For EGFR-mutant LUAD, Osimertinib therapy faces the nearly inevitable development of acquired resistance, and its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. By integrating clinical data, organoid models, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), we confirmed that integrin subunit beta 8 (ITGB8) was highly expressed in LUAD and strongly correlates with poor prognosis and reduced response to Osimertinib. ScRNA-seq analysis revealed a dominant paracrine axis between ITGB8 + cancer cells and POSTN-expressing cancer-associated fibroblasts (POSTN + CAFs). Employing extensive in vitro and in vivo approaches, we established that CAF-derived POSTN drives LUAD malignancy and acquires resistance via a novel compartmentalized dual mechanism. This dual mechanism involves exosomal POSTN being internalized by ITGB8 + cancer cells, where it directly binds to and activates mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling. In parallel, secreted POSTN engages the cell surface ITGB8 receptor to initiate the canonical focal adhesion kinase (FAK)/proto-oncogene tyrosine-protein kinase Src (Src)/protein kinase B (AKT) signaling cascade. Consequently, targeting the POSTN-ITGB8 axis effectively suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, and reverses Osimertinib resistance. Overall, our study unveils a novel crosstalk axis that promotes LUAD progression and Osimertinib resistance, providing a compelling rationale for developing combination therapies co-targeting POSTN and ITGB8.

title: ACQ-based hybrid nanocrystals enable particokinetics assessment and unravel the in vivo fate of meloxicam nanocrystals
abstract: The clinical translation of nanocrystal-based nanomedicines is significantly hindered by the lack of suitable methods for particokinetic analysis, as conventional techniques are unable to track intact nanocrystals quantitatively. The hybrid nanocrystal (HNC) technique, which incorporates aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) probes into the crystal lattice without affecting its intrinsic properties, offers a promising alternative by generating a fluorescence signal that diminishes upon nanocrystal dissolution. This fluorescence change can thus be utilized to quantify nanocrystal concentrations. In this study, meloxicam (MLX) HNCs were fabricated to mimic key characteristics of Anjeso®, including size, crystallinity, dissolution behavior, and pharmacokinetics. The correlation between fluorescence quenching and nanocrystal dissolution was first confirmed in vitro , while a fluorescent calibration curve was established for the quantification of MLX-HNCs. Following intravenous administration in rats, particokinetics were assessed via blood fluorescence. The particokinetic profile deviated from the pharmacokinetic curve (based on plasma MLX concentration) after 2h, indicating gradual nanocrystal dissolution. Only 4.1% of MLX was released within 2h, increasing to 28.8% by 4h. Fluorescence imaging revealed prolonged nanocrystal retention in the mononuclear phagocyte system (MPS) for up to 24h, consistent with slow dissolution. This sustained release profile, likely mediated by protein corona formation, explains the delayed onset and insufficient late-stage analgesia of Anjeso®. The ACQ-based HNC technique thus provides a proof-of-concept methodology for direct particokinetic evaluation, offering crucial insights into nanocrystal fate in vivo and establishing a framework applicable to similar nanocarrier systems.

title: Artificial agonists for receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs): Design, classification, and therapeutic potential
abstract: : Receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), as core regulatory elements in cell signal transduction, play a critical role in maintaining physiological homeostasis. Imbalances in their activity are closely associated with tumorigenesis, metabolic disorders, and neurodegenerative diseases. Despite significant advancements in the development of RTK inhibitors over the past four decades, the therapeutic potential of strategies targeting RTK activation remains underexplored in regenerative medicine, metabolic disorders, and immune dysregulation. Physiological activation of RTKs is essential for tissue repair and the maintenance of metabolic homeostasis. Artificially designed RTK agonists can precisely modulate receptor activity by mimicking natural ligands or employing innovative molecular engineering approaches, offering a novel avenue for disease treatment. This review systematically examines the design, classification, and therapeutic potential of artificial RTK agonists, elucidating their unique mechanisms of action from four types of agents acting as agonists: peptides, DNA, small molecule compounds, and antibodies. Furthermore, it provides a theoretical foundation and practical guidance with clinical translational potential for the development of next-generation, highly efficient RTK agonists.

title: Loganin ameliorates acetaminophen-induced acute liver injury via targeting TOP1MT˗mediated hepatocyte apoptosis and ferroptosis
abstract: Abstract Acetaminophen (APAP) overdose can cause severe liver injury, and new drugs are urgent needed for effective treatment. Small molecules in Chinese medicine have long been a treasured reservoir for drugs screening. Here, we reported that loganin (LOG), an active ingredient in Corni Fructus, exerts hepatoprotective effects as indicated by potently alleviated liver damages in APAP-induced liver injury (AILI) murine model. LOG reversed the decreased SOD, GSH and CAT levels, and reduced lipid peroxidation, ROS production, and iron overload and hence reduced apoptosis/ferroptosis of hepatocytes of AILI models, as apoptosis/ferroptosis inducers abolished, whereas their inhibitors enhanced the effect of LOG. Through the activity-based proteome profiling (ABPP) clickable alkyne-tagged LOG probe, mitochondrial topoisomerase I (TOP1MT) was captured as a direct target of LOG, which was further validated by CETSA and ITC assays. Deficiency of TOP1MT significantly compromised the effects of LOG on H2O2-induced oxidative stress cell model via regulating downstream apoptosis/ferroptosis regulators Bax, Bcl-2, NRF2, GSH, SLC7A11, and GPX4. Consistently, LOG effect was greatly eliminated in AILI mice once the endogenous hepatic TOP1MT was knocked-down by AAV-TOP1MT shRNA. Thus, TOP1MT might be a potential target for AILI treatment and LOG represents one of the most promising candidate drugs or lead compounds.

title: Panax quinquefolius derived extracellular vesicles promote post-chemotherapy immune reconstitution through the remodeling functions of macrophages via the NOD2/RIP2 axis
Dimethyl fumarate inhibits keratinocyte hyperproliferation and ameliorates psoriasis via directly targeting ribosomal protein S6 kinase A1
abstract: Background: Dimethyl fumarate (DMF) is a widely used first-line treatment for psoriasis due to its proven efficacy and irreplaceable therapeutic effects. Keratinocyte (KC) hyperproliferation is a central pathogenic feature of psoriasis. However, the precise mechanisms by which DMF regulates KC hyperproliferation remain poorly understood.Methods: We employed an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced mouse model of psoriasis to evaluate the in vivo efficacy of DMF, alongside multiple inflammatory factors-induced HaCaT cells to assess the effect of DMF on KC proliferation in vitro. Using streamlined cysteine activity-based protein profiling (SLC-ABPP), surface plasmon resonance (SPR), molecular docking, and active-site mutation analysis, we aimed to to clarify the specific target of DMF and its key binding site. Immunoprecipitation (IP) coupled with mass spectrometry (MS)/Western blot (WB), and kinase activity assay were employed to identify and evaluate the effect of DMF on the interacting protein of its target. Flow cytometry technology, WB, immunofluorescence staining, and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) were employed to assess the effect of DMF on mitophagy.Findings: Through a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments, we demonstrated that DMF feectively suppressed KC hyperproliferation in psoriasis both in vivo and in vitro. We identified that DMF exerts its effects by directly targeting the Cys432 site of Ribosomal Protein S6 Kinase A1 (RSK1). DMF suppresses RSK1 kinase activity, leading to the dephosphorylation of its downstream substrate protein-ATP/ADP translocase 1 (ANT1), This, in turn, diminishes ANT1-PTEN induced putative kinase 1 (PINK1)-Parkin axis-mediated mitophagy. Importantly, epidermis-specific RSK1 knockdown in mice results in the inhibition of KC hyperproliferation in psoriasis, an effect that could not be further influenced by DMF treatment.Interpretation: Our study reveals a novel mechanism by which DMF targets RSK1 to suppress KC hyperproliferation in psoriasis, offering new insights into its therapeutic efficacy. Furthermore, our results establish RSK1 as a potential therapeutic target for psoriasis treatment.

title: Systematic analysis reveals the action mechanisms and medicinal implications of latroeggtoxin-VI
abstract: Latrodectus spp. spiders, most often called black widow spiders, are one of the most venomous spiders known in the world. Different from many other venomous animals, Latrodectus spp. spiders have toxic components not only in their venom glands, but also in other parts of the adult spider body, newborn spiderlings and even the eggs. Latroeggtoxin-VI (LETX-VI), a bioactive peptide found from the eggs of spider Latrodectus tredecimguttatus, has been shown to extensively affect the metabolic processes in nerve cells via multiple action mechanisms. Due to its abilities to promote the synthesis, transport and release of dopamine, down-regulate the expression of α-synuclein, inhibit excessive inflammation, protect nerve cells, transmembrane deliver drugs, etc., LETX-VI is suggested to have application prospects in combating diabetes mellitus and central nervous system disorders such as Parkinson′s disease and depression. This review presents our understanding of the LETX-VI, including its properties, structure, action mechanisms, and potential applications. It should be pointed out that: i) almost all currently available data on LETX-VI have been generated by a single research group, and there are no independent replications; ii) no direct pharmacokinetic or quantitative blood-brain barrier penetration measurements, and no systematic in vivo dose-response studies; and iii) therefore, all therapeutic implications discussed in this review should be regarded as highly preliminary and hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory.

title: Sculponeatin A promotes SMURF1-mediated KLF5 degradation and disrupts KLF5/c-Myc co-liquid-liquid phase separation to inhibit aerobic glycolysis in gastric cancer
abstract: Targeting glycolytic reprogramming presents a novel strategy for anticancer drug development. Sculponeatin A (sptA), a natural diterpenoid compound isolated from Isodon sculponeatus , exhibits potent antitumor activity. This study elucidates the mechanism by which sptA suppresses glucose metabolic reprogramming in gastric cancer (GC) through targeted degradation of Krüppel-like factor 5 (KLF5) and disruption of its co-phase separation with cellular myelocytomatosis oncogene (c-Myc). We demonstrate that sptA effectively inhibits GC proliferation. RNA-sequencing analysis revealed that sptA suppresses glycolysis and downregulates the c-Myc pathway in GC cells. Using the drug affinity responsive target stability - mass spectrometry approach, we identified KLF5 as a direct binding target of sptA. Mechanistic studies show that sptA inhibits c-Myc-mediated aerobic glycolysis by directly binding to KLF5. This binding disrupts the KLF5/c-Myc interaction and their co-liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) within the nucleus, while concurrently promoting Smad ubiquitination regulatory factor 1-mediated ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation of KLF5, ultimately inhibiting glucose metabolic reprogramming in GC cells. This work systematically delineates the pharmacological mechanism whereby sptA exerts antitumor effects by targeting KLF5/c-Myc co-LLPS to inhibit glycolytic reprogramming, providing a crucial foundation for developing small-molecule inhibitors targeting KLF5 phase separation.

title: System pharmacology reveals the mechanism of Puji Xiaodu Yin against Japanese encephalitis
abstract: Japanese encephalitis (JE) caused by the JE virus (JEV) lacks specific therapeutics. Puji Xiaodu Yin (PJXDY) is a classic formula used for acute and critical illnesses; however, its effects and mechanisms in the treatment of JE remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the pharmacological effects of PJXDY, identify its representative active components, and explore underlying mechanisms. A JE mouse model was established by subcutaneous injection of JEV into the footpad. The therapeutic effects of PJXDY were evaluated by survival rates, behavioral changes, viral load assays, inflammatory factor levels, and histopathological staining. Brain-accessible components were identified using ultra performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole-time of flight-mass spectrometry/mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS). System pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vitro assays were employed to screen for representative active components with the strongest activities. Drug affinity responsive target stability, bio-layer interferometry, enzyme activity assays, small interfering RNA (siRNA), Western blot, and immunofluorescence were used to explore mechanisms. PJXDY dose-dependently increased survival, improved neurological symptoms, reduced viral loads, and alleviated brain damage. Three representative active components were selected: antiviral rosmarinic acid (RA), anti-inflammatory cosmosiin (CAA), and 3,5,6,7,8,3',4'-heptamethoxyflavone (HMF) inhibiting PANoptosis-like cell death. Mechanistic studies suggested that they were associated with non-structural protein 5 methyltransferase domain (NS5 MTase), mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase 1 (MEK1), and Z-DNA binding protein 1 (ZBP1), respectively, correlating with reduced viral replication, suppressed inflammatory cytokine production, and diminished PANoptosis-related marker expression. The three-component combination showed efficacy comparable to that of PJXDY. This study lays an experimental foundation for the clinical application and modern development of PJXDY.

title: A facile antibody-mediated CMC platform for targeted screening of CCR1 ligands from Magnolia officinalis
Editorial Board
Nanoscavenger-enabled clearance of thrombospondin-1 protects the neurovascular unit after cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is a major cause of secondary brain damage following ischemic stroke, characterized by persistent neurovascular dysfunction and inflammatory amplification. Increasing evidence suggests that extracellular pathogenic proteins released after ischemic insult continue to damage the neurovascular unit during reperfusion; however, most existing therapeutic strategies focus on receptor blockade rather than active elimination of these extracellular mediators. Here, we report an engineered nanoscavenger system designed to selectively intercept and clear thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1), a matricellular protein critically involved in endothelial injury and blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption after cerebral ischemia-reperfusion. By functionalizing biodegradable nanoparticles with a TSP-1-binding ligand, the nanoscavengers efficiently capture extracellular TSP-1 in ischemic brain tissue, prevent its pathological interaction with endothelial receptors, and promote its systemic redistribution and lysosome-associated processing after macrophage uptake. In murine models of CIRI, nanoscavenger treatment significantly reduced TSP-1 accumulation in the ischemic brain, preserved BBB integrity, and protected the structural and functional integrity of the neurovascular unit. This material-enabled clearance strategy attenuated endothelial apoptosis, suppressed neuroinflammation, and resulted in improved neurological outcomes without inducing systemic toxicity. Collectively, this study demonstrates that nanoscavenger-enabled extracellular protein clearance represents an effective materials-based strategy for mitigating cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. These findings highlight the potential of engineered nanomaterials to achieve spatiotemporally controlled elimination of pathogenic extracellular proteins in neurovascular and inflammatory disorders.

title: Artificial intelligence reshaping the gout diagnosis and treatment paradigm
abstract: Gout is a systemic inflammatory disease characterized by the deposition of monosodium urate crystals. Its inherent pathophysiological complexity and intricate comorbidity network pose increasing challenges to clinical management. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a potential paradigm shift in addressing this complexity. This review systematically reviews key applications of AI in gout management, including imaging-based diagnostic enhancement, multisource data fusion for risk identification, and intelligent analysis of clinical text. AI further supports comprehensive comorbidity management, encompassing cardiovascular and renal risk assessment as well as gut microbiota modulation, and assists in optimizing treatment strategies through integrated clinical parameters. In drug development, AI accelerates target identification and safety prediction. Although challenges related to methodological rigor and data privacy remain, multimodal AI integration offers a clear technological roadmap toward precision medicine in gout and highlights the critical role of interdisciplinary collaboration in clinical translation.

title: Natural products for combatting antibiotic-resistant Gram-negative bacteria: Role, mechanism, and future direction
abstract: Gram-negative bacteria (GNB) infection therapy poses a significant challenge in the field of infectious diseases due to their extensive resistance to clinically advanced antibiotics such as carbapenems and third-generation cephalosporins, and novel therapeutic options are urgently needed. Unlike single-target antibiotics, natural products derived from herbs exert therapeutic effects through synergistic mechanisms, including bacterial growth inhibition, modulation of inflammatory pathways, and regulation of microbial balance and host immune function. In this review, we systematically summarized natural products that have demonstrated promising efficacy against drug-resistant GNB. We highlighted several widely used natural product formulations with validated therapeutic outcomes through rigorous clinical trials, including Tanreqing injection (TRQ) and Xuebijing injection (XBJ). The active constituents of these natural products and their mechanisms of action are thoroughly discussed, providing valuable insights into the potential of natural products for developing combinational anti-drug-resistant GNB agents. Moreover, an overview of opportunities and challenges in achieving standardized quality control, multi-target/antibiotic synergy, exploration of molecular mechanisms of action, and clinical practice transformation. Finally, this review summarizes the key challenges in the clinical translation of natural products and emphasizes the importance of advancing multi-target/antibiotic synergistic therapies, establishing standardized quality control protocols, and elucidating molecular mechanisms of action.

title: Nanophotonic biosensing for prostate cancer diagnosis and monitoring: Strategies and intelligent systems
abstract: Nanophotonic biosensing is driving transformative advances in interdisciplinary fields such as precision medicine and environmental monitoring, thanks to its outstanding sensitivity, real-time response, and strong integration capabilities. Prostate cancer (PCa) represents the second most common malignancy in men worldwide. Current diagnostic methods, including prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing, imaging, and invasive procedures, still face significant limitations in early screening and recurrence monitoring. This review focuses on the challenges in the early diagnosis of PCa, starting with the classification and the research progress of nanophotonic biosensing technologies. It further elaborates on their significant contributions to liquid biopsy and dynamic monitoring for PCa. Additionally, we further incorporate artificial intelligence (AI)-driven data processing and system-level integration, highlighting applications in early diagnosis, personalized treatment selection, and prognostic surveillance. Finally, we examine the clinical prospects and prevailing challenges of AI-enhanced nanophotonic biosensing, aiming to provide insightful perspectives and a solid foundation for future research.

title: PB2 alleviates diabetic nephropathy: Intervene gut-flora-dependent metabolite TMAO promote DN-associated inflammatory responses through ferroptosis, ER stress–autophagy axis, and macrophage polarization
abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN), a condition characterized by persistent inflammatory responses, represents one of the most serious complications of diabetes mellitus; however, effective treatment strategies for DN remain limited. This study aimed to explore the potential therapeutic effects of procyanidin B2 (PB2) in mice with DN induced by high-fat diet (HFD) and streptozotocin (STZ). Tissue pathology was evaluated by histopathological analysis. Microbiome sequencing, targeted metabolomics, quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT‒PCR), western blotting (WB), and immunohistochemistry (IHC) were combined to explore alterations in gut-derived trimethylamine N -oxide (TMAO) and the underlying mechanisms through which PB2 in prevents DN. Finally, TMAO rescue experiment and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) was performed to validate the regulatory effects of TMAO and the gut microbiota on DN. The results indicated that PB2 significantly improved liver and kidney function and intestinal-barrier integrity via the gut–liver–kidney axis while maintaining cholesterol homeostasis and restoring bile acid (BA) metabolism. Notably, PB2 significantly modulated the gut microbiota and markedly decreased circulating TMAO levels by targeting the trimethylamine/flavin-containing monooxygenase 3/TMAO axis. TMAO promoted renal injury by multiple signaling pathways, thereby inducing ferroptosis, stress–autophagy axis, macrophage polarization. Furthermore, TMAO supplementation and FMT verified the importance of the gut-flora-dependent metabolite TMAO in the protective role of PB2 against DN. Collectively, these findings clarify the anti-DN effects of PB2, which occur through a novel gut–liver–kidney axis-based mechanism, and suggest that PB2 is a promising therapeutic option for DN through the modulation of kidney inflammation.

title: Pharmacometrics-driven dose individualization of modified-release formulations: integration of PopPK, PBPK, and PK/PD modeling
abstract: Modified-release (MR) formulations improve adherence and therapeutic consistency by controlling drug release; however, prolonged, formulation-dependent absorption produces complex, multiphasic pharmacokinetics that complicate dose selection, bioequivalence assessment, and clinical optimization. Pharmacometrics, integrating population pharmacokinetics (PopPK), physiologically based pharmacokinetics (PBPK), and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling, provides a quantitative framework for characterizing formulation-controlled inputs, distinguishing absorption from disposition processes, and quantifying interindividual variability across oral, transdermal, and long-acting injectable (LAI) platforms. Within drug development, model-informed drug development (MIDD) applies PBPK models to link in vitro release and physiology with systemic exposure, enabling mechanistic prediction of food effects, organ impairment, and drug–drug interactions, while PopPK models identify variability drivers and define population-based initial dosing regimens that inform labeling. Formulation optimization and virtual bioequivalence are achieved by simulating alternative release profiles and exposure metrics against predefined regulatory criteria, enabling prospective evaluation of scenarios beyond feasible clinical testing. MIDD and model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) represent distinct but sequential stages along a translational continuum: MIDD establishes evidence-based population dosing strategies during development, whereas MIPD operationalizes validated PopPK/PBPK models as Bayesian priors, integrates patient-specific therapeutic drug monitoring data, and individualizes dosing in real time. Emerging hybrid PBPK-PopPK frameworks, machine learning (ML)-assisted covariate discovery, and tissue-aware digital twins further enhance predictive performance. Collectively, these pharmacometric approaches provide a translational bridge linking MR formulation design, regulatory evaluation, and individualized therapy.

title: A tensor decomposition approach for missing data imputation and dimensionality reduction in longitudinal microbiome data
Spatial metabolic fluxes reveal tissue metabolic heterogeneity by integrating mass spectrometry imaging and stable isotope tracing
abstract: The integration of mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) with stable isotope tracing enables in situ tracking of metabolic activities within heterogeneous biological tissues. However, accurately quantifying metabolic reactions in spatially resolved isotope tracing analyses remains a major challenge. Here, we present MSIFluxer, a user-friendly and automated tool for spatial metabolic flux analysis. MSIFluxer automatically identifies 13 C-labeled metabolites, corrects for natural isotope abundances, and calculates labeling fractions from MSI data. It then employs an optimization algorithm to fit the extensive isotopic labeling datasets, thereby determining relative metabolic fluxes across different metabolic pathways. This approach allows for a detailed elucidation of tissue-specific metabolic activities, the turnover fluxes of labeled metabolites, and the direction of reversible reactions. Using MSIFluxer, we mapped central carbon metabolism fluxes across rat kidney, brain, and clinical tumor samples. Quantitative metabolic flux analyses revealed faster glutamate and glutamine turnover in the kidney medulla, active tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycling and energy production in the cerebral cortex (CTX), and distinct activation of the pentose phosphate pathways (PPPs) in laryngeal cancer. Together, these results highlight MSIFluxer as a powerful tool for in situ quantitative characterization of metabolic heterogeneity within and across biological tissues.

title: Dual-mechanism driven adsorption on silica microspheres enables precision pharmacokinetic profiling of liposomal therapeutics
Novel β-Cyclodextrin–BINAM composite chiral stationary phases: Synergistic dual-site chiral recognition revealed by tailored chiral probes
abstract: 1,1'-Binaphthyl-2,2'-diamine (BINAM) and β -cyclodextrin ( β -CD) are widely used chiral selectors (CSs), yet chiral stationary phases (CSPs) based on a single selector often exhibit limited enantioselectivity. Here, we report a class of composite CSPs (AMCDP1–5) fabricated by modifying β -CD with axially chiral S/R -BINAM selectors. The accurate structure was confirmed by characterization methods such as single-crystal X-ray diffraction, elemental analysis, and thermogravimetric analysis. The enantioseparation performance of these CSPs was evaluated with 41 commercial/natural chiral drugs and 60 synthetically designed chiral probes under reversed-phase and polar mobile-phase High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) conditions. Compared with single chiral selectors (individual BINAM derivatives or native β -CD), the composite CSPs exhibited pronounced synergistic effects (“1+1>2”). For several analytes, superior resolution and broader separation scope were achieved relative to commercial β -CD (EnantioPak® SDMP) and polysaccharide-based columns (CHIRALPAK® IB), particularly for phenylurea and thiourea racemates. Based on extensive enantioseparation data, the chiral recognition mechanism of the novel CSPs was investigated from both the stationary phase and analyte perspectives using molecular docking simulations. It was found that ( S )-configured BINAM and CSPs bearing electron-withdrawing substituents exhibited superior chiral recognition. For chiral analytes, aromatic rings or amide groups are indispensable for the enantioseparation; electron-donating substituents and para -benzene or β -naphthalene substitution sites consistently lead to enhanced enantioseparation efficiency. Mechanistic studies reveal that high-resolution enantioseparation is critically dependent on a synergistic dual-site recognition model, involving both β -CD cavity inclusion and BINAM-facilitated hydrogen bonding/π–π stacking interactions. The separation performance improves as the temperature decreases, reaching its optimum when the retention factor ( k ) is in the range of 3–5. Applied to antifungal agents (isoconazole nitrate and tioconazole), AMCDP2 successfully resolved their enantiomers, which exhibited distinct antifungal activities.

title: Droplet-based microfluidics: Emerging detection assays and their transformative potential in biomedicine
abstract: The unique features of droplet-based microfluidics including automation, minimal reagent consumption, and high throughput make it a powerful analytical platform for life science applications such as single-cell analysis, tissue engineering, drug discovery, and healthcare. However, the accuracy, convenience, and efficiency of analyzing samples within droplets significantly influence the broader adoption of droplet microfluidics in both traditional scientific and industrial contexts. To break through the bottleneck of droplet-device universalness, researchers persist in discovering more powerful analysis methods and suitable biochemical applications for droplet microfluidics in recent decades. In this review, we summarize traditional and emerging detection methods, such as optical spectrometry, mass spectrometry (MS), and droplet separation, as well as cutting-edge applications including dynamic cell/tissue analysis, single-cell sequencing, drug screening, pharmaceuticals microsphere fabrication, wearable healthcare, and spatial omics. Finally, we discuss and outlook the transformative potential of small-volume droplet systems in addressing challenging biological and chemical questions, and highlight how advances in droplet-based analytical assays are paving the way for innovative solutions.

title: Serum MRGPRX2 identifies an IgE-independent subgroup of allergic rhinitis
abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a prevalent inflammatory disorder located in the nasal tissues, imposing a substantial global disease burden. Current diagnostic methods detect allergic sensitization but lack the capacity to discriminate subgroups, limiting the precision of therapeutics. Serum levels of Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 (MRGPRX2), elevated in allergic conditions, remain unvalidated as an AR biomarker. We hypothesized that serum MRGPRX2 serves as a novel diagnostic biomarker enabling subgroup-driven AR management. We enrolled 213 seasonal AR patients and 113 matched healthy controls at the hospital and quantified serum MRGPRX2 levels using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, and binary logistic regression was used to estimate the odds ratio for AR risk. AR cases had higher MRGPRX2 levels (69.84 vs. 40.67 ng/mL, P < 0.001). Although the area under the curve (AUC) for MRGPRX2 (0.77) was lower than that of total IgE (0.85), it remained a significant predictor. At a cut-off of 39.11 ng/mL, the sensitivity was 85.45%. Furthermore, patients with severe AR exhibited significantly higher MRGPRX2 levels compared to those with mild/moderate AR ( P < 0.01). The correlation between serum MRGPRX2 and total IgE levels was weak ( r = 0.264, P < 0.001), revealing a distinct clinical subgroup characterized by low serum total IgE but elevated MRGPRX2 (14.08% of cohort). Thus, serum MRGPRX2 is a promising diagnostic biomarker for AR, capable of stratifying patients, particularly identifying an IgE-low/MRGPRX2-high subgroup. This putative subgroup may require alternative treatment approaches targeting MRGPRX2-mediated pathways.

title: Targeting the YAP:TEAD domain through fluorescence-anisotropy displacement assay
abstract: Interface 3 of the YAP:TEAD complex a key Hippo pathway effector driving oncogenesis. • A robust fluorescence anisotropy displacement assay was developed using an Ω-loop peptide probe to identify TEAD4 Interface 3 inhibitors. • Successful probe displacement by pyrazolopiperidone inhibitors confirms the assay’s suitability for hit and lead screening.

title: KRAS mutations in gastrointestinal cancers: New insights from pathogenic mechanisms to therapeutic challenges
abstract: Kirsten rat sarcoma virus ( KRAS ) mutations comprise approximately 85% of rat sarcoma virus ( RAS ) alterations and occur in more than 90% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDACs) and over 40% of colorectal cancers (CRCs). Although KRAS-G12C inhibitors have transformed a target long considered undruggable, most gastrointestinal (GI) tumours harbour non-G12C alleles and remain constrained by intrinsic, acquired and adaptive resistance and by an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TME). This review synthesizes allele- and disease-specific biology and epidemiology; delineates immune vulnerabilities created by KRAS-driven remodelling of the TME; and appraises emerging modalities with near-term clinical relevance, including next-generation allele-specific and pan-KRAS inhibitors, RAS degraders, KRAS-directed T cell receptor (TCR) therapies and neoantigen vaccines. We integrate genomic, signalling and clinical evidence to define primary, acquired and adaptive resistance archetypes and map them to rational combination strategies. By translating rapidly evolving biology into practice-oriented guidance, this review outlines opportunities to extend benefit beyond KRAS-G12C, overcome resistance, inform trial design and improve real-world decision-making for patients with KRAS -mutant GI malignancies.

title: Recent advances in metal–drug self-assembled nanomedicines: Carrier-free strategies for multifunctional cancer therapy
abstract: Carrier-free nanomedicines constructed through metal–ligand coordination have emerged as a promising paradigm for cancer therapy, offering ultra-high drug loading, simplified formulation, and intrinsic responsiveness to tumor microenvironments. These assemblies exploit therapeutic molecules and metal ions as both structural and functional components, integrating catalytic activity, redox regulation, immune modulation, and imaging capability within a single supramolecular platform. This review summarizes recent progress in coordination-driven self-assembly, including the roles of phenolic, carboxylate, multidentate, and other ligand-bearing small molecules in generating stable, stimuli-responsive nanostructures. Particular emphasis is placed on the unique biological functions of representative metal ions for ferroptosis-/cuproptosis-inducing therapies, endoplasmic reticulum calcium flux-mediated apoptosis, cyclic GMP–AMP synthase (cGAS)–stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signalling pathway-dependent immune activation, etc. Emerging strategies that incorporate multiple drugs or multiple metals into one carrier-free nanoparticle are also highlighted, enabling synergistic multimodal therapy and integrated diagnostics. Finally, we discuss current challenges and outline future opportunities for coordination-based carrier-free nanomedicines to advance precision oncology.

title: Editorial Board
Self-assembled materials based on traditional Chinese medicine active ingredients for antibacterial and wound healing applications
abstract: As the largest organ of the human body, the skin presents significant challenges in treating infections following injury. Statistical analysis of literature over the past five years reveals a marked upward trend in the number of publications, with alkaloids, polyphenols, hydrogels, and nanoparticles (NPs) emerging as current research hotspots. Distinct from conventional reviews, this article is the first to systematically integrate, from a multidimensional mechanistic perspective, the synergistic effects of self-assembled materials derived from traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in terms of multifunctional integration and modulation of the wound microenvironment. Nevertheless, critical analysis indicates that existing research still faces bottlenecks, including insufficient component specificity, poor solubility, and uncertain feasibility for large-scale production. This review aims to provide a theoretical foundation for the development of integrated antimicrobial and regenerative wound therapies.

title: Leveraging Ecotoxicity Parameters and Machine Learning to Rethink the Drug Discovery Pipeline
abstract: This study introduces a modular computational workflow integrating ecotoxicological parameters into the early stages of antiparasitic drug discovery. Using a curated library of 497 Trypanosoma brucei -active compounds, we combined a machine learning-based SAFE/UNSAFE classifier with a composite scoring system, the GreenDrugScore (GDS), which merges pharmacokinetic (ADMETscore), ecotoxicological (ECOscore), and drug-likeness (DLscore) properties. The classifier, trained on 1,464 annotated molecules, achieved strong performance (ROC-AUC = 0.85) and identified 267 SAFE compounds. Incorporation of ecotoxicological endpoints, bioaccumulation (BCF), protozoan growth inhibition (IGC 50 ), and aquatic toxicity (LC 50 for Daphnia magna and Fathead minnow ), reshaped prioritization, with 28.5% of compounds being deprioritized due to unfavourable predicted ECO profiles. Scaffold analysis of top-ranked compounds identified 19 chemotypes with predicted environmentally favourable profiles, combining low predicted bioaccumulation with high aquatic LC 50 /IGC 50 values. Overall, these results support the utility of early ecotoxicological integration as a decision-oriented strategy for prioritizing candidate scaffolds under One Health perspective.

title: Application of cerebral microdialysis to evaluate drug transport efficacy from nose to brain affected by cerebral fluid clearance
Karyoptosis prevents the proliferation of colon cancer cells via p21/Rb-dependent and p53-independent signaling pathways
DNA Tetrahedron-Confined Localized CHA for Rapid and Multiplex miRNA Sensing toward Live-Cell Imaging and Clinical Cancer Diagnostics
abstract: Achieving precise, multi-target profiling of intracellular microRNAs (miRNAs) is pivotal for cancer stratification but is hindered by the kinetic sluggishness and potential signal crosstalk of conventional diffusion-based probes. To overcome these barriers, we engineered a spatially segregated, dual-color logic gate anchored on a discrete DNA tetrahedron (DTN). Distinct from aggregation-based assays that rely on intermolecular assembly, this platform utilizes strict intramolecular nanoconfinement. By stoichiometrically positioning two orthogonal catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) modules at a defined proximity of approximately 14.6 nm, we induce a 2.54 × 10 6 -fold surge in effective local molarity. This design drives ultrafast strand displacement kinetics while maintaining the nanostructure in a monodispersed state, which is critical for efficient cellular uptake. The resultant DTN-confined localized CHA (DTN-LCHA) system operates as a leakage-free “nanolab-on-a-particle”, enabling carrier-independent cytosolic delivery via caveolae-mediated endocytosis. Consequently, the system allows for the simultaneous, ratiometric imaging of miR-21 and miR-31, successfully discriminating breast cancer subtypes and validating clinical serum samples with high fidelity. This work presents a generalizable paradigm for engineering non-interfering, high-speed molecular circuits for accurate disease phenotyping.

title: Mannan-oligosaccharides-based self-assembly nanoparticles enable gut-specific quercetin release, providing multi-pathway protection against AD via gut-brain axis
abstract: Mannan-oligosaccharides (MOS), as indigestible functional prebiotic, support intestinal health. Here, we engineered MOS to undergo linoleic acid (LA)-mediated self-assembly with quercetin, forming lipid bilayer nanoparticles (MOS-LA/LA-Q NPs). These nanoparticles achieved a high quercetin encapsulation efficiency (92.4%) and demonstrated superior stability in aqueous solution at 4 °C. The MOS outer layer effectively protected the quercetin core from gastrointestinal stress. Triggered by microbial enzymes, the system enabled a sustained quercetin release, up to 60% over 48 h, representing a novel microbe-specific delivery mechanism. In an Alzheimer’s disease (AD) mice models induced by AlCl 3 /D-galactose, MOS-LA/LA-Q NPs significantly enhanced gut microbiota diversity, restored gut microbiota balance, suppressed pathogenic bacteria, and regulated metabolites short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) and lactic acid levels. Compared with free quercetin, these nanoparticles (NPs) alleviated cognitive deficits, reduced inflammation and oxidative stress in both the colon and brain, improved gut-brain barrier integrity, and restored gut-brain function more significantly. Mechanistically, these effects were associated with modulation of the kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (Keap1)/nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) and toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB) pathways, reducing tau phosphorylation and Aβ amyloid levels, thus demonstrating superior neuroprotection. This study proposes a novel strategy for addressing the complex pathology of AD through multi-target intervention, highlighting the potential of MOS-based NPs to enhance quercetin’s therapeutic efficacy.

title: Charged-tagging ion-exchange chromatography enables rapid, accurate and comprehensive (RAC) profiling of free thiols and charge heterogeneity in mAbs
abstract: Free thiol content and charge heterogeneity are critical quality attributes for therapeutic antibodies, impacting stability, activity, and batch consistency. Currently, no single analytical method can simultaneously profile both attributes in a rapid, accurate, and comprehensive manner, especially with the ability to distinguish between exposed and buried free thiols. Here, we present a novel charged-tagging strategy using N-2-aminoethyl maleimide, a thiol-specific derivatizing agent that introduces a defined positive charge upon conjugation. This enables clear separation by ion-exchange chromatography while preserving the inherent capability to resolve charge heterogeneity. For exposed free thiols, direct labeling provides excellent resolution and quantitative recovery. For buried or partially buried thiols, a mild structural-unfolding step enables quantitative derivatization while preserving native charge profiles. Implemented on a standard high performance liquid chromatography-ultraviolet detector (HPLC-UV) system, this platform delivers the first integrated, rapid, accurate and comprehensive-compatible approach for simultaneous free thiol and charge heterogeneity profiling. Our work significantly expands the detection ability of ion-exchange chromatography and offers a practical solution for mAb process development, optimization, and routine quality control.

title: Development and comparison study of automated tangential flow filtration coupled with electrophoresis for the simultaneous isolation of extracellular vesicles
Deep-pert: A deep ensemble learning framework for interpretable unveiling drug mechanisms and prioritizing synergistic target pairs from perturbation profiles
Berberine derivative B4 alleviates ulcerative colitis via dual HSP60/NLRP3 targeting to restore mitochondrial homeostasis and suppress inflammasome activation
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic and recurrent inflammatory bowel disease. Current therapeutic strategies achieve clinical remission in only 30%–60% of patients, indicating the crucial need for safer and more effective treatment options. Mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and immune dysregulation are critically involved in UC pathogenesis. The NOD-like receptor pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome, a key regulator of innate immunity, disrupts immune homeostasis disruption when aberrantly activated. In this study, we identified a berberine (BBR) derivative B4, which demonstrated markedly superior efficacy over the parent compound BBR in ameliorating dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced UC mouse model, along with a favorable safety profile. Mechanistic studies revealed that B4 exerts its effects through dual targeting. B4 directly binds to heat shock protein 60 (HSP60), effectively reversing mitochondrial redox and metabolic imbalance, reducing reactive oxygen species (ROS) burst and HSP60 translocation, thereby suppressing NLRP3 activation at the source on one hand. Furthermore, B4 directly targets the NLRP3 protein to inhibit inflammasome assembly, which significantly reducing the secretion of interleukin-1beta (IL-1β) and interleukin-18 (IL-18), and suppressing pyroptosis. This dual-targeting synergy effectively interrupts the vicious positive feedback loop of “mitochondrial dysfunction-NLRP3 inflammasome activation-exacerbated inflammation-aggravated mitochondrial damage,” indicating that B4 is a promising therapeutic agent for UC. Moreover, this novel strategy of co-targeting the “mitochondria-NLRP3 inflammasome axis” provides a new direction for UC drug development.

title: Editorial Board
Disturbing mitochondrial functionalities on the utilization of Lenvatinib-conjugated Gallium (III) nanocomposites as therapeutic avenue to potentiate hepatocellular carcinoma inhibition
abstract: Lenvatinib, an effective treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), faces limitations due to mitochondrial function shift-induced energy metabolism reprogramming. Therefore, interfering with mitochondrial energy metabolism to enhance the curative effect of lenvatinib may represent a promising strategy. In this study, an indocyanine green (ICG)-templated self-assembling nanotherapeutic, lenvatinib-Ga (LGa), containing lenvatinib and gallium (III) ions, was constructed for combination therapy of HCC. LGa significantly enhanced the ability to induce HCC cell death. Subsequent investigations into mitochondrial dysfunction revealed that LGa increased intracellular levels of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), leading to the collapse of mitochondrial membrane potential, impairments in adenosine triphosphate (ATP) synthesis and cellular respiration, as well as downregulation of Bcl-2 and activation of cleaved-caspase 3. Additionally, LGa upregulated endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress-related protein expression (activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4), eukaryotic initiation factor 2 alpha (EIF2α), and C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP)), boosting calcium ion (Ca 2+ ) overload. These effects promoted HCC cell apoptosis and suppressed tumor growth in vivo . Moreover, LGa was further able to induce immunogenic cell death (ICD), promoting dendritic cell (DC) maturation. Simultaneously, LGa promoted the release of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), activating the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling pathway and subsequently triggering a DC-mediated immune response. Combined with anti-PD-1 antibody immunotherapy, LGa achieved synergistic anti-tumor effects. Our findings suggest LGa could be a promising therapeutic approach for HCC.

title: Visualizing mitochondrial peroxynitrite and high-content screening of peroxynitrite scavengers in liver cells with a glycosylated iridium(III)-based probe
abstract: Peroxynitrite (ONOO − ) is a highly reactive species with potent oxidative properties that plays a crucial role in signal transduction. Abnormal levels of ONOO − can lead to a variety of diseases, including acute liver injury. Hence, ONOO − scavengers are emerging as potential bioactive molecules for combating acute liver injuries. However, the development of simultaneously water-soluble, selective and sensitive probes for subcellular ONOO − levels remains challenging, and there is also a lack of reliable and informative screening methods for ONOO − scavengers. In this work, we reported a luminescent iridium(III)-based probe with a 1,4:3,6-dianhydro-α- D -glucopyranose (DGP)-derived hydrazone as the recognition unit of ONOO − . The incorporation of DGP improved the aqueous solubility of the iridium(III) complex compared to the parent specie, from 7.80 × 10 −3 g/L to 1.44 × 10 −2 g/L. Moreover, the probe showed high sensitivity for ONOO − , with a detection limit (LOD) of as low as 0.14 μM. Finally, this probe was capable of detecting both exogenous and endogenous ONOO − in mitochondria in liver cells, and also demonstrated good penetration (approximately 75.6 μm) in 3D tumor spheroids. Leveraging its sensing merits, the probe was successfully applied for high-content screening (HCS) of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drugs, identifying fezolinetant as an ONOO − scavenger. Taken together, this work provides a useful imaging tool for probing ONOO − functions and diagnosing liver injury, and also offers the first HCS platform for ONOO − scavengers, holding great promise for the diagnosis and therapy of ONOO − -related diseases in the future.
